artists.biography:
Therapy? are a rock band from Northern Ireland. The band was formed in 1989 by guitarist-vocalist Andy Cairns from Ballyclare and drummer-vocalist Fyfe Ewing. Therapy? recorded their first demo with Cairns filling in on bass guitar. To complete the lineup, the band recruited Larne bassist Michael McKeegan. The band signed with major label A&M Records in 1992, for which they released four albums, most notably Troublegum in 1994 and Infernal Love in 1995. Ewing's departure in early 1996 preceded the arrivals of his replacement Graham Hopkins, and Martin McCarrick on cello and guitar. Neil Cooper replaced Hopkins on drums in 2002. Following the departure of McCarrick in 2004, the band have remained a stable three-piece since.

Therapy? are currently signed to UK independent label Marshall Records. The band has released 15 full-length studio albums and has sold over two million albums worldwide.

perplexity.description:
Therapy?'s Greatest Hits (The Abbey Road Session), released in 2020 on Marshall Records, is a career-spanning collection that reimagines 12 of the band's UK Top 40 hits, recorded live at the legendary Abbey Road Studios. The album showcases Therapy?'s signature blend of alternative rock, punk, and melodic hard rock, with the live setting adding a fresh, dynamic energy to their best-known tracks. The performances highlight the band's tight musicianship and enduring songwriting, capturing the raw power and emotional depth that have defined their sound since their formation in 1989.

As a milestone release coinciding with Therapy?'s 30th anniversary and their "So Much for the 30 Year Plan Tour," this album serves as both a retrospective and a celebration of the band's legacy. It stands apart from their studio albums by offering new interpretations of classic songs, rather than simply compiling original recordings. While not a commercial blockbuster, the album was well-received by fans and critics for its authenticity and the quality of the live renditions, reinforcing Therapy?'s reputation as one of Ireland's most resilient and influential rock acts.
